subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should this umbrella remain the canonical multi-agent stability tracker while the narrower session-lock, delivery, auth, and detached-work repairs are reviewed, or should maintainers split the remaining work into separate canonical issues now?
rationale: Current main has partial fixes and multiple open candidate repairs, but the remaining cancellation/scheduling/recovery semantics are a maintainer product and ownership decision rather than a safe automatic cleanup close.

options.title: Keep the umbrella until narrow fixes settle
options.body: Use this issue as the active coordination point while reviewing the linked focused PRs and issues, then close it once the remaining slices are proven fixed or explicitly split.

options.title: Split now into canonical sub-issues
options.body: Move each remaining symptom to a narrower canonical issue and close this umbrella only after every unique log and production scenario is linked to the new owners.

options.title: Defer broader orchestration direction
options.body: Keep only strict bug fixes active and route token-ring or manager-style orchestration proposals to separate product/RFC review.

recommendation.title: Keep the umbrella until narrow fixes settle
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the active coordination point while reviewing the linked focused PRs and issues, then close it once the remaining slices are proven fixed or explicitly split.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for subagent delivery, session lock, and config mutation ownership points to steipete, and the decision is about how to split or sponsor the remaining product work.
